stories.headline: Lai Ching-te completes surprise Eswatini visit after China-backed overflight blockade
stories.summary: President Lai Ching-te arrived in Eswatini on May 2 — Taiwan's sole African diplomatic ally — after an earlier April trip was cancelled when Seychelles, Mauritius, and Madagascar revoked overflight permits under alleged Chinese pressure. Germany and the Czech Republic also denied European transit requests. Lai travelled aboard an Eswatini royal charter aircraft, met King Mswati III, signed a customs cooperation agreement, and delivered bilateral pledges on agriculture, energy, and cultural ties. China condemned the visit as a 'stowaway-style escape farce' and called Lai a 'rat'; Taiwan's MOFA defended the approach as consistent with international diplomatic precedent.

stories.headline: TSMC 2nm expansion accelerates: five fabs ramping, Arizona packaging plant confirmed, ASML High-NA EUV deferred
stories.summary: TSMC's North America Technology Symposium 2026 in Silicon Valley disclosed that five 2nm fabrication facilities are simultaneously entering volume production this year, with capacity projected to grow 70% compound annually through 2028 — outpacing 3nm ramp by 45%. The company confirmed it will skip ASML's High-NA EUV tools for its upcoming A13 and A12 nodes, citing cost; a chip packaging facility in Arizona via Amkor is targeted for pre-2029 opening. Investor and analyst commentary around record Q1 revenues (US$35.9B, 66.2% gross margin) and Taiwan's stock market surpassing Canada to become the world's sixth-largest by market cap drove heavy coverage across tech and financial media.

stories.headline: Taiwan tops Beijing's agenda for upcoming Trump-Xi summit; China warns US to 'make the right choices'
stories.summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi, in a call with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, explicitly named Taiwan as the 'biggest risk point' in US-China relations, urging Washington to make correct choices ahead of President Trump's planned Beijing visit later in May. Multiple Reuters and Guardian analyses flagged concern that Trump's transactional approach and desire for a trade deal could lead to a softening of US positions on Taiwan. Taiwan's government formally expressed concern following the call, and Beijing's soft-power messaging — including focus on President Lai's ancestral clan village in Fujian — was covered in parallel.

stories.headline: KMT internally divided over special defense budget; party pressures lawmakers as TPP stays undecided
stories.summary: Taiwan's KMT opposition party remained split over the government's NT$1.25 trillion special defense budget proposal, with the KMT caucus backing a counter-proposal of NT$800 billion tied to formal US Letters of Offer and Acceptance (LOAs), while a faction led by a deputy chair threatened to expel Legislative Speaker Han Kuo-yu for reportedly supporting the NT$800B plan. KMT Chairwoman Cheng Li-wun stated the budget amounts to a 'blank check' and refused approval without confirmed arms procurement agreements; the Taiwan People's Party remained undecided. Cross-party negotiations were scheduled for May 6 with a floor vote targeted for May 8.

stories.headline: TSMC trade secrets case: Tokyo Electron fined $5M, former engineer sentenced to 10 years
stories.summary: A Taiwanese court handed down its harshest ruling yet in a semiconductor technology theft case on April 27, sentencing Chen Li-ming — a former TSMC engineer who moved to Tokyo Electron's Taiwan subsidiary — to 10 years in prison for stealing 2nm process trade secrets in violation of Taiwan's National Security Act. Tokyo Electron's local unit was fined NT$150 million (approximately US$5 million); three other TSMC employees received sentences of two to six years. TSMC reaffirmed zero-tolerance policy for trade secret violations.

stories.headline: TSMC divests full Arm Holdings stake for US$231 million
stories.summary: TSMC, through its subsidiary TSMC Partners, sold its remaining 1.11 million Arm Holdings shares between April 28-29 at an average of US$207.65 per share, realising approximately US$231 million and fully exiting the investment it took in connection with Arm's 2023 Nasdaq IPO. The transaction generated roughly US$174 million in retained earnings; analysts noted the divestment restores TSMC's position as a fully neutral foundry partner as Arm moves toward its own silicon production. TSMC described the exit as a routine financial portfolio adjustment.

stories.headline: KMT chair plans June US trip, requests Trump meeting; party context from April Xi Jinping visit
stories.summary: KMT Chairwoman Cheng Li-wun confirmed she has requested a meeting with US President Trump during a planned June trip to Washington, where she also intends to meet think tanks and Taiwanese diaspora groups. The visit comes weeks after Cheng travelled to Beijing and met President Xi Jinping in April — the first KMT leader to do so in a decade. An academic commentary linked the KMT-CPC dialogue to cross-strait stability framing.

stories.headline: KMT-TPP select joint New Taipei City mayoral candidate for upcoming election
stories.summary: Former Taipei Deputy Mayor Lee Shu-chuan of the KMT was selected as the joint KMT-TPP candidate for New Taipei City mayor after defeating TPP Chairman Huang Kuo-chang in a coordination poll. The joint nomination consolidates the two opposition parties' electoral cooperation ahead of the local elections.

stories.headline: US-Philippines showcase NMESIS anti-ship missiles near Taiwan in annual war games
stories.summary: US and Philippine forces demonstrated the NMESIS anti-ship missile system in Batanes Province — approximately 100 miles south of Taiwan — during the annual Balikatan joint exercises. Maritime strike drills were also conducted in Itbayat municipality, highlighting the strategic Luzon Strait corridor as a focus of allied military posturing amid cross-strait tensions.

stories.headline: TSMC investor activity: stock reaches near-record highs; institutional holdings and analyst commentary
stories.summary: Following TSMC's Q1 2026 earnings beat (revenue US$35.9B, +35% YoY; gross margin 66.2%), institutional investor activity and analyst commentary proliferated across financial media. Billionaires Druckenmiller and Cramer were cited as holders; Verity Asset Management trimmed its stake; and multiple outlets noted TSMC's stock approaching all-time highs. Analyst comparison with Intel and attention to TSMC's AI-driven revenue concentration dominated retail investor commentary.

stories.headline: PLA conducts 29-aircraft incursion near Taiwan, 15 sorties crossing median line
stories.summary: Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense reported detecting 29 Chinese military aircraft sorties, six PLAN vessels, and two official ships operating around Taiwan on May 2. Fifteen of the aircraft crossed the median line and entered Taiwan's northern, central, and southwestern ADIZ, conducting what Beijing described as air-sea joint training.
